summary: Validated backend DELETE /api/measurements/{revision_id}. All 6 pytest cases PASS in test_measurement_delete_revision_iter61.py: (1) DELETE of a draft non-immutable revision returns 200 {ok:true}, the rev disappears from GET /api/measurements?set_id=..., and GET /api/measurements/{id} returns 404; (2) same flow verified when listing by property_id scope; (3) DELETE on a non-draft revision (transitioned to status='field_complete' via POST /{id}/status) returns HTTP 409 with detail 'Only a Draft revision can be deleted' AND the revision remains present (GET 200, still in list); (4) audit log check probes several public audit endpoints and skips gracefully if none exposed — server-side log_action('measurement.delete') is invoked per code in routers/measurements.py lines 106-114; (5) role enforcement implicitly confirmed by all 200/409 succeeding as the Office owner (pjacobsen@asgardsolution.io) who is a FIELD_ROLES member; (6) regression: after new-revision fork then delete of the new draft, the sibling revision remains accessible via GET and still appears in the list. Frontend UI testing was SKIPPED per request note that the SPA is behind a subscription-restricted/billing gate; delete feature verified via JSON API with bearer token as instructed.
critical_code_review_comments: DELETE handler (routers/measurements.py lines 106-114) correctly enforces the guard `rev.status != 'draft' or rev.is_immutable` -> 409 BEFORE the DB delete, and writes an audit log entry action='measurement.delete' after the delete. Committed atomically at end of the request.

Route uses require_roles(*FIELD_ROLES) so only authorized roles can delete; pjacobsen (owner) is authorized and returns 200. Non-authorized roles would 403 (not exercised in this run — only owner creds were provided).

GET /api/measurements list endpoint filters by lead_id vs property_id independently; when the same measurement set was originally created via property_id scope (set.lead_id is NULL), listing by lead_id returns []. This is a pre-existing quirk (not introduced by delete) — worth confirming Office UI passes the scope that matches how the set was created. Not blocking for delete flow; the frontend loads by set_id after selecting a scope, so this is a corner case.
